components.note: 卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'

用 is traditionally read as a picture of a wooden stake fence, or by another theory a bucket — either way an early ideograph whose form was borrowed to represent the abstract sense 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 病人每天要按时服用两次药。
example.pinyin: bìngrén měitiān yào ànshí fúyòng liǎng cì yào.
example.english: The patient must take the medicine on time twice a day.
example.fact: Penicillin, the first true antibiotic, was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 after he noticed mold accidentally contaminating a petri dish had killed the surrounding bacteria; it entered widespread medical use in the 1940s and dramatically reduced deaths from bacterial infection during World War II.

components.note: The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
忄 (heart) — 惜 describes an emotional response felt in the heart.
昔 (the past, former times) — feeling 忄 for the past 昔 gave 惜 its meaning 'to cherish, to regret.'

example.hanzi: 他不惜一切代价去救那只受伤的小狗。
example.pinyin: tā bùxī yīqiè dàijià qù jiù nà zhī shòushāng de xiǎo gǒu.
example.english: He spared no cost to save the injured little dog.
example.fact: Wolves, the ancestors of domestic dogs, were first tamed by humans at least 15,000 years ago, making dogs the oldest domesticated animal — genetic evidence suggests some early dog lineages may even predate the rise of agriculture.

components.note: 发 is the simplified form of 發, which combined a bow being drawn with a pair of hands releasing an arrow — motion sent off in a burst, extended to mean 'to send out, to issue,' and by extension 'hair' (fà), which grows out from the body.
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'

example.hanzi: 老板因为报告迟交而对他发火了。
example.pinyin: lǎobǎn yīnwèi bàogào chí jiāo ér duì tā fāhuǒ le.
example.english: The boss got angry at him because the report was late.
example.fact: Anger triggers a surge of adrenaline and cortisol that raises heart rate and blood pressure within seconds; researchers have found that chronic anger and hostility are linked to a measurably higher risk of heart disease over a person's lifetime.

components.note: 礻 (spirit) — 祷 concerns communicating with the spirits or gods.
寿 (shòu) gives a sound distantly related to dǎo, having drifted apart over time.
口 (mouth) — the act of speaking.
牛 (ox) — traditionally read as speaking with the forceful weight of an ox, giving 告 its meaning 'to tell, announce, inform.'

example.hanzi: 每天晚上,奶奶都会安静地祷告。
example.pinyin: měitiān wǎnshàng, nǎinai dōu huì ānjìng de dǎogào.
example.english: Every night, grandma quietly prays.
example.fact: The oldest known written prayers come from ancient Sumer, inscribed in cuneiform on clay tablets more than 4,000 years ago, addressed to deities like Enlil and Inanna asking for protection, health, and good harvests.

components.note: 卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
力 (effort, strength) sits at the base of 务 — the character relates to tasks or affairs that require exertion, as in 服务 'to serve' or 任务 'task.'
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 服务员,请给我们一壶热茶。
example.pinyin: fúwùyuán, qǐng gěi wǒmen yī hú rè chá.
example.english: Waiter, please bring us a pot of hot tea.
example.fact: Tipping is believed to have originated in 17th-century England, where wealthy patrons at coffeehouses would give small coins "to insure promptness" before their meal even arrived; the custom later spread to the United States after the Civil War.

components.note: 犭 (dog/animal) — historically linked to a wary, hesitant animal, extended to mean 'as if, similar to.'
尤 (yóu) is an exact match for the sound of 犹.
象 (elephant) — elephants once roamed the region now called Henan, tying the character to comfort and abundance.
予 (yǔ) gives the sound — a close match for yù, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 面对两份工作机会,她犹豫了很久。
example.pinyin: miànduì liǎng fèn gōngzuò jīhuì, tā yóuyù le hěn jiǔ.
example.english: Facing two job offers, she hesitated for a long time.
example.fact: Buridan's ass is a philosophical paradox describing a hungry donkey placed exactly between two identical piles of hay, so perfectly balanced by reason that it cannot choose either and starves — used since the Middle Ages to illustrate the danger of excessive deliberation.

components.note: 永 is traditionally read as a picture of branching tributaries flowing from a main river — a channel that divides and continues on, giving rise to the character's meaning 'perpetual, forever.'
Heart — relates to inner feeling, like steady determination.
Suggests something extending continuously, like a constant state.

example.hanzi: 钻石常被用来象征永恒的爱情。
example.pinyin: zuànshí cháng bèi yòng lái xiàngzhēng yǒnghéng de àiqíng.
example.english: Diamonds are often used to symbolize eternal love.
example.fact: Diamonds form under intense heat and pressure roughly 150 to 200 kilometers below Earth's surface and are carried upward by volcanic eruptions; most of the diamonds mined today were forged more than a billion years ago, long before complex life existed on land.

components.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.
匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 他们相识之后,从此成了最好的朋友。
example.pinyin: tāmen xiāngshí zhīhòu, cóngcǐ chéngle zuì hǎo de péngyou.
example.english: After they met, they became best friends from then on.
example.fact: Charles Darwin and the botanist Joseph Hooker met in 1839 and remained close friends and scientific confidants for over 40 years; Hooker was one of the few people Darwin trusted with an early draft of his theory of evolution long before "On the Origin of Species" was published in 1859.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
介 (jiè) gives a sound hint — 价 is pronounced jià, sharing the same initial consonant though the vowel has shifted.

example.hanzi: 拍卖会上,他为那幅画出价十万元。
example.pinyin: pāimài huì shàng, tā wèi nà fú huà chūjià shí wàn yuán.
example.english: At the auction, he bid a hundred thousand yuan for that painting.
example.fact: In 2017, Leonardo da Vinci's painting "Salvator Mundi" sold at a Christie's auction for $450.3 million, making it the most expensive painting ever sold publicly — the final bid came after roughly 19 minutes of competing offers.

meanings: to dismiss students at the end of the school day

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.

example.hanzi: 孩子们放学后喜欢在操场上打篮球。
example.pinyin: háizimen fàngxué hòu xǐhuan zài cāochǎng shàng dǎ lánqiú.
example.english: After school lets out, the kids like to play basketball on the field.
example.fact: Basketball was invented in December 1891 by physical education instructor James Naismith in Springfield, Massachusetts, who nailed two peach baskets to a gymnasium balcony and wrote thirteen original rules to keep his students active during the cold New England winter.

components.note: 礻 (spirit/altar) — ancestor worship at a family altar ties 祖 to the spirit radical.
且 (qiě) gives a sound distantly related to zǔ, having drifted apart over time.
乂 depicts a hand gripping a tool.
八 here depicts a hand-axe — a father shown wielding a tool to provide for and protect the family gave 父 its meaning 'father.'

example.hanzi: 我祖父年轻时是一名木匠。
example.pinyin: wǒ zǔfù niánqīng shí shì yī míng mùjiang.
example.english: My grandfather was a carpenter when he was young.
example.fact: The oldest confirmed woodworking joints, found at Israel's Jaljulia archaeological site, date back roughly 9,000 years, showing that carpentry techniques like mortise-and-tenon joinery are almost as old as settled agriculture itself.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'

example.hanzi: 时间不早了,我们回见吧。
example.pinyin: shíjiān bù zǎo le, wǒmen huíjiàn ba.
example.english: It's getting late, see you later then.
example.fact: The first mechanical clocks with escapements appeared in medieval European monasteries around the 13th century, built primarily to ring bells calling monks to prayer at consistent hours — a technology that eventually reshaped how all of society organized its day.

components.note: 弓 here pictures a young, bent shoot rather than a bow.
冫 (ice/frost) repeated twice suggests two young shoots wilting in the cold, giving 弱 its meaning 'weak, fragile.'
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 每个超级英雄都有自己的弱点。
example.pinyin: měi gè chāojí yīngxióng dōu yǒu zìjǐ de ruòdiǎn.
example.english: Every superhero has their own weak point.
example.fact: In Greek mythology, the warrior Achilles was said to be invulnerable everywhere except his heel, the one spot his mother forgot to submerge in the river Styx — giving rise to the modern term "Achilles' heel" for a single critical vulnerability.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 愚人节那天,他跟同事开了一个恶作剧。
example.pinyin: yúrénjié nà tiān, tā gēn tóngshì kāile yī gè èzuòjù.
example.english: On April Fools' Day, he played a practical joke on his coworker.
example.fact: April Fools' Day's exact origin is debated, but one leading theory ties it to France's 1564 shift from the Julian calendar, which began the new year around April 1, to the Gregorian calendar starting January 1 — those who kept celebrating on the old date were mocked as "April fools."

components.note: A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
车 (cart) — 载 means to carry or transport by vehicle.
哉 (zāi) gives a rhyme close to zài, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 请先下载这个应用程序再打开它。
example.pinyin: qǐng xiān xiàzǎi zhège yìngyòng chéngxù zài dǎkāi tā.
example.english: Please download this app first before opening it.
example.fact: The first file ever transferred over what became the internet was sent in 1969 between two computers at UCLA and Stanford Research Institute, roughly 500 kilometers apart; the system crashed after only the first two letters of "LOGIN" were successfully transmitted.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — honey is made by bees, which are insects.
宓 (mì) gives the sound — an exact match for 蜜.
月 is a simple picture of a crescent moon.

example.hanzi: 他们打算去巴厘岛度蜜月。
example.pinyin: tāmen dǎsuàn qù bālí dǎo dù mìyuè.
example.english: They plan to spend their honeymoon in Bali.
example.fact: Bali's iconic terraced rice paddies rely on a centuries-old irrigation system called subak, a cooperative water-sharing network managed by farmer communities and temple priests that UNESCO recognized as a World Heritage Site in 2012 for embodying a philosophy of harmony between humans, nature, and the spiritual realm.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 投 relates to throwing something with the hand
殳 (shū) gives a loose sound connection to 投's reading tóu
讠 (speech) — represents words being spoken.
斥 (to reprimand, blame) — words of accusation or complaint gave 诉 its meaning 'to sue, to tell, to complain.'

example.hanzi: 顾客向经理投诉了食物的质量问题。
example.pinyin: gùkè xiàng jīnglǐ tóusù le shíwù de zhìliàng wèntí.
example.english: The customer complained to the manager about the quality of the food.
example.fact: The world's oldest known consumer complaint is a nearly 3,750-year-old clay tablet from ancient Babylon, in which a customer named Nanni complained to a copper merchant named Ea-nasir that the copper delivered was of poor quality and the wrong grade.

components.note: Bird — an older semantic root kept from an earlier character shape.
Gives the sound hù, related to gù but drifted apart over time.
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'

example.hanzi: 这家公司有超过五百名雇员。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu chāoguò wǔbǎi míng gùyuán.
example.english: This company has more than five hundred employees.
example.fact: The Ford Motor Company's decision in 1914 to pay assembly-line workers $5 a day — roughly double the prevailing wage — cut worker turnover dramatically and is often credited with helping create a stable American middle class able to afford the very cars it built.

components.note: 月 is a simple picture of a crescent moon.
亮 is traditionally read as a picture of a lit oil lamp raised on a stand, radiating light — a fitting image for its meaning 'bright, radiant.'

example.hanzi: 今晚的月亮特别圆特别亮。
example.pinyin: jīnwǎn de yuèliang tèbié yuán tèbié liàng.
example.english: Tonight's moon is especially round and bright.
example.fact: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year, a measurement possible because Apollo astronauts left retroreflectors on the lunar surface that scientists still bounce laser beams off today.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
八 (two hands) — holding something up.
目 (a container/tray) — held between the two hands, the image behind 具's meaning 'tool, utensil.'

example.hanzi: 新买的家具还没有送到我家。
example.pinyin: xīn mǎi de jiājù hái méiyǒu sòngdào wǒ jiā.
example.english: The furniture I just bought hasn't been delivered to my home yet.
example.fact: IKEA's flat-pack furniture concept began in 1956 when an employee named Gillis Lundgren removed the legs from a table so it would fit into his car, sparking the idea that shipping furniture unassembled could drastically cut transport costs and space.

components.note: 人 (a man) — the figure straining upward.
止 (feet) — standing up on his feet, or toes, to look into the distance, the image of anticipation giving 企 its meaning 'to look forward to, hope for' and, by extension, 'enterprise' (企业).

业 is the simplified form of 業, originally a picture of a wooden rack with jagged teeth used to hang bells or chime-stones in ancient orchestras; the idea of an ongoing, structured undertaking broadened over time to mean 'work, occupation, industry.'

example.hanzi: 这家企业去年的利润增长了三成。
example.pinyin: zhè jiā qǐyè qùnián de lìrùn zēngzhǎng le sān chéng.
example.english: This company's profits grew by thirty percent last year.
example.fact: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, is considered the world's first publicly traded corporation; at its peak it issued its own currency, maintained a private army of roughly 10,000 soldiers, and its shares traded on what became the first formal stock exchange, in Amsterdam.

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 狮 names an animal, the lion.
师 (shī) gives the sound — an exact match with 狮.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 动物园里的狮子正在晒太阳。
example.pinyin: dòngwùyuán lǐ de shīzi zhèngzài shài tàiyáng.
example.english: The lion at the zoo is sunbathing.
example.fact: A lion's roar can be heard from up to 8 kilometers away, produced by a specialized flat, square-shaped larynx and vocal cords that let air pass through with less resistance than in other big cats, generating the lowest, loudest roar of any cat species.

components.note: 方 here depicts a flag or banner, marking a group on the move.
氏 depicts a person following behind — together, a group traveling together, giving 旅 its meaning 'trip, journey.'
辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 这次长途旅途让他学到了很多东西。
example.pinyin: zhè cì chángtú lǚtú ràng tā xuédào le hěn duō dōngxi.
example.english: This long journey taught him a lot.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway, completed in 1916, stretches over 9,289 kilometers between Moscow and Vladivostok, making it the longest single railway line in the world — a full end-to-end journey takes about seven days and crosses eight time zones.

meanings: climax (of a story, a competition etc)

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
氵 (water) — 潮 names the rise and fall of the sea, the tide.
朝 (cháo) is an exact match for the sound of 潮.

example.hanzi: 电影的高潮部分让观众紧张得不敢呼吸。
example.pinyin: diànyǐng de gāocháo bùfen ràng guānzhòng jǐnzhāng de bùgǎn hūxī.
example.english: The climax of the movie made the audience so tense they could barely breathe.
example.fact: Ocean tides are caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon combined with the Sun's weaker pull; the Bay of Fundy in Canada experiences the largest tidal range on Earth, with water levels rising and falling by as much as 16 meters between high and low tide.

components.note: 卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'
人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.

example.hanzi: 士兵必须无条件服从命令。
example.pinyin: shìbīng bìxū wútiáojiàn fúcóng mìnglìng.
example.english: Soldiers must obey orders unconditionally.
example.fact: The 1961 Milgram experiment at Yale University found that roughly 65% of ordinary participants were willing to administer what they believed were painful electric shocks to a stranger simply because an authority figure in a lab coat instructed them to continue, revealing how strongly situational authority can override personal conscience.

components.note: 直 (straight, upright) — 真 relates to something level and true.
几 (a small table) — an object placed level and true on a table gave 真 its meaning 'real' or 'true.'
讠 (speech) — 诚 relates to speaking honestly and sincerely.
成 (chéng) gives the sound — an exact match with 诚's reading chéng.

example.hanzi: 他用真诚的态度向大家道歉。
example.pinyin: tā yòng zhēnchéng de tàidù xiàng dàjiā dàoqiàn.
example.english: He apologized to everyone with a sincere attitude.
example.fact: Psychologists have found that a genuine "Duchenne smile" — named after the 19th-century French neurologist Guillaume Duchenne who first studied it — involves involuntary contraction of the muscles around the eyes, not just the mouth, which is why fake smiles are often detectable even to casual observers.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one speaking.
言 (speech, words) — a person's spoken word being reliable and true gave 信 its meaning 'trust, faith, letter.'
今 (now, the present) — represents what is currently on one's mind.
心 (heart/mind) — keeping the present moment in mind gave 念 its meaning 'to think of, to read aloud, to study.'

example.hanzi: 坚定的信念帮助她度过了最困难的时期。
example.pinyin: jiāndìng de xìnniàn bāngzhù tā dùguò le zuì kùnnán de shíqī.
example.english: Her firm conviction helped her get through the most difficult period.
example.fact: Ernest Shackleton's crew survived nearly two years stranded in Antarctica after their ship Endurance was crushed by ice in 1915; historians often credit their survival to Shackleton's unshakeable belief that he would bring every one of his 27 men home alive, which he ultimately did.

components.note: 亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'
口 (mouth) — 嘴 refers directly to the mouth, or a beak-like spout.
觜 (zī) gives a sound distantly related to zuǐ, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: “住嘴!”妈妈生气地喊道。
example.pinyin: “zhùzuǐ!” māma shēngqì de hǎn dào.
example.english: "Shut up!" mom shouted angrily.
example.fact: The human vocal cords can vibrate anywhere from about 60 to 1,000 times per second depending on pitch, and sustained shouting at high volume can cause tiny tears in the vocal fold tissue, which is why singers and voice coaches train people to project sound using breath support rather than throat strain.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ancient texts were written on bound bamboo strips, and 第 originally referred to the sequential order of such strips, giving rise to its meaning 'ordinal number' (as in 第一, first).
Two lines curving apart from each other, originally meaning 'to divide, split' — the shape was later adopted to represent the number 'eight.'

example.hanzi: 这是他第八次参加马拉松比赛。
example.pinyin: zhè shì tā dì bā cì cānjiā mǎlāsōng bǐsài.
example.english: This is the eighth time he has taken part in a marathon.
example.fact: The modern marathon distance of 42.195 kilometers wasn't standardized until the 1908 London Olympics, when organizers extended the course so the race could start at Windsor Castle and finish in front of the royal box at the stadium — the odd extra 195 meters has stuck ever since.

meanings: variant of 老家伙[lao3 jia1 huo5]

components.note: 耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
亻 (person) — 伙 relates to people who share meals or work together.
火 (huǒ) gives the sound — an exact match with 伙's reading huǒ.

example.hanzi: 那个老家伙每天都在公园里下棋。
example.pinyin: nàge lǎojiāhuo měitiān dōu zài gōngyuán lǐ xiàqí.
example.english: That old fellow plays chess in the park every day.
example.fact: Chess is believed to have originated in northern India around the 6th century AD as a game called chaturanga, which spread through Persia and the Islamic world before reaching Europe by the 9th century, evolving along the way into the version played today.

components.note: A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'
火 (fire) — 焰 names part of a fire, the flame.
臽 (xiàn) gives a sound close to yàn, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 蜡烛的火焰在风中轻轻摇晃。
example.pinyin: làzhú de huǒyàn zài fēng zhōng qīngqīng yáohuàng.
example.english: The candle's flame swayed gently in the wind.
example.fact: A candle flame appears blue at its base and yellow-orange at its tip because temperature varies sharply within it — the blue zone near the wick can exceed 1,400°C where combustion is most complete, while the visible yellow glow higher up comes from glowing, unburned soot particles.

components.note: 立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'
乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'
人 (people) over 云 (clouds/say) — a picture of people gathering and speaking together, related to 会's meanings 'to meet' and 'to know how to.'

example.hanzi: 我们昨晚去听了一场古典音乐会。
example.pinyin: wǒmen zuówǎn qù tīng le yī chǎng gǔdiǎn yīnyuèhuì.
example.english: We went to a classical music concert last night.
example.fact: The Vienna Philharmonic's New Year's Concert, held every January 1st since 1939, is broadcast to more than 90 countries and an estimated audience of tens of millions, making it one of the most widely watched classical music events in the world.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 温 originally described warm water.
昷 (wēn) gives the sound — an exact match with 温.
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 今天的温度比昨天低了很多。
example.pinyin: jīntiān de wēndù bǐ zuótiān dī le hěn duō.
example.english: Today's temperature is much lower than yesterday's.
example.fact: The lowest natural air temperature ever recorded on Earth's surface was -89.2°C, measured at Vostok Station in Antarctica in July 1983 — cold enough that exhaled breath can freeze into tiny ice crystals that make a faint hissing sound, an effect Siberians call "the whisper of stars."

components.note: 木 (wood) — 极 originally named the ridgepole, the highest beam of a roof, extended to 'extreme, utmost.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 极 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 长时间加班让他感到极度疲惫。
example.pinyin: cháng shíjiān jiābān ràng tā gǎndào jídù píbèi.
example.english: Working overtime for a long time left him feeling extremely exhausted.
example.fact: The longest documented period without sleep in a controlled study is about 11 days, endured by 17-year-old Randy Gardner in 1964 under scientific observation; researchers noted severe effects on his mood, concentration, and short-term memory well before that point, which is why such experiments are no longer conducted today.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.
辶 (to walk, movement) — 通 relates to passing through or getting somewhere.
甬 (yǒng) gives a hint of the sound — 通 is pronounced tōng, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 请稍等,我马上帮您接通电话。
example.pinyin: qǐng shāo děng, wǒ mǎshàng bāng nín jiētōng diànhuà.
example.english: Please wait a moment, I'll connect your call right away.
example.fact: The first transatlantic telephone cable, TAT-1, was completed in 1956 between Scotland and Newfoundland, carrying just 36 simultaneous voice channels — a stark contrast to modern fiber-optic cables that can carry many terabits of data per second across the same ocean.

components.note: 市 is traditionally read as a picture of a flag or cloth banner hung above a stall to mark a trading spot — the image behind its meaning 'market, city.'
巳 (here representing an eye) — in one traditional theory, this depicted a captive's marked eye, an ancient sign of subjugation, which later broadened to mean 'the common people.'
戈 (a dagger-axe) — combined with the eye shape above, this ties the character to the idea of marking or piercing.

example.hanzi: 政府呼吁市民节约用水。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ hūhū shìmín jiéyuē yòngshuǐ.
example.english: The government is calling on city residents to conserve water.
example.fact: Cape Town, South Africa, came close to running out of municipal water entirely during a severe 2017-2018 drought, prompting the city to plan for a "Day Zero" when taps would be shut off; strict conservation by residents that cut usage nearly in half ultimately helped the city avoid the shutoff.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water that is deep.
罙 (deep) — combined with water, giving 深 its meaning 'deep.'
氵 (water) — the water that is deep.
罙 (deep) — combined with water, giving 深 its meaning 'deep.'

example.hanzi: 她深深地吸了一口气,然后开始演讲。
example.pinyin: tā shēnshēn de xī le yī kǒu qì, ránhòu kāishǐ yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: She took a deep breath and then began her speech.
example.fact: Freedivers competing without fins or breathing apparatus have descended past 100 meters on a single breath; the current world record for "no-limits" freediving exceeds 214 meters, a depth at which the human lungs compress to roughly a quarter of their surface volume under the pressure.

components.note: 生 (growth, to sprout) — young plants pushing up from the ground.
The lower element pictures a well or a pit of mineral pigment; combined with new growth above, the two together evoke the blue-green color of fresh plants, giving 青 its meaning 'blue-green, young.'
少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 很多青少年喜欢在社交媒体上分享生活。
example.pinyin: hěn duō qīngshàonián xǐhuan zài shèjiāo méitǐ shàng fēnxiǎng shēnghuó.
example.english: Many teenagers like to share their lives on social media.
example.fact: Neuroscientists have found that the human prefrontal cortex, the brain region responsible for planning and impulse control, doesn't fully mature until around age 25 — a finding that has reshaped how researchers understand risk-taking behavior during adolescence.

components.note: 白 — a shining crown
王 (king) — the ruler wearing the crown
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.

example.hanzi: 皇家花园每年只对外开放几天。
example.pinyin: huángjiā huāyuán měinián zhǐ duìwài kāifàng jǐ tiān.
example.english: The royal garden is only open to the public a few days each year.
example.fact: The gardens of the Palace of Versailles took over 40 years and the labor of tens of thousands of workers to complete under Louis XIV, and the fountains were engineered with such complex hydraulics that a special canal was dug to divert water from the Seine just to keep them running.

components.note: 贝 (shell money, wealth) sits on the left.
有 (to have) — paired with wealth 贝, this pictures someone possessing money improperly, giving 贿 its meaning 'to bribe.'
贝 depicts a cowrie shell, used as ancient currency — it marks the character as related to money or valuables.
各 means 'each, individual'; combined with 'money,' it evokes money changing hands to an individual, giving 赂 its meaning 'to bribe.'

example.hanzi: 那名官员因受贿赂而被判入狱。
example.pinyin: nà míng guānyuán yīn shòu huìlù ér bèi pàn rùyù.
example.english: The official was sentenced to prison for accepting bribes.
example.fact: Transparency International has published its Corruption Perceptions Index every year since 1995, ranking over 180 countries by perceived levels of public-sector corruption — a tool now widely used by investors, aid agencies, and researchers to compare governance quality worldwide.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 基 relates to the ground or foundation something is built on.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 基 is pronounced jī, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 这个项目基本上已经完成了。
example.pinyin: zhège xiàngmù jīběnshang yǐjīng wánchéng le.
example.english: This project is basically finished already.
example.fact: The Pareto principle, formulated by Italian economist Vilfredo Pareto in 1896 after he observed that roughly 80% of Italy's land was owned by 20% of the population, is now applied across fields from business to software engineering to describe how a small share of causes basically accounts for most outcomes.

components.note: 尸 (here representing a covering or stall, not a corpse) — 展 pictures a place where goods are displayed.
衣 (clothing) — clothing laid out for display gave 展 its meaning 'to unfold' or 'to exhibit.'
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

example.hanzi: 消防队立即展开了搜救行动。
example.pinyin: xiāofáng duì lìjí zhǎnkāi le sōujiù xíngdòng.
example.english: The fire brigade immediately launched a search and rescue operation.
example.fact: The James Webb Space Telescope's sunshield, made of five ultra-thin layers of a material called Kapton, had to unfold in space using more than 100 release mechanisms after its 2021 launch — a process so complex that engineers called it one of the most technically risky deployments ever attempted.

components.note: 后 originally pictured a ruler issuing a command with an open mouth, and was used for 'queen, empress'; after simplification it also absorbed the unrelated character 後 ('behind, after'), which is why 后 today can mean both 'queen' and 'back, rear.'
台 is traditionally read as a picture of a raised earthen platform or mound. After simplification it also stands in for 臺 and 檯, giving it the modern meanings 'platform, stage, stand.'

example.hanzi: 演出结束后,演员们都聚在后台聊天。
example.pinyin: yǎnchū jiéshù hòu, yǎnyuánmen dōu jù zài hòutái liáotiān.
example.english: After the show ended, the actors all gathered backstage to chat.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House took 14 years to complete and its final cost of about $102 million was roughly 1,400% over the original 1957 budget estimate, largely because of the building's technically demanding stage machinery and sail-like roof structure.

components.note: 上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two
扌 (hand) — relates directly to 拉's meaning 'to pull, drag,' an action done by hand.
立 (lì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted noticeably from lā.

example.hanzi: 周末我们常常去唱卡拉OK。
example.pinyin: zhōumò wǒmen chángcháng qù chàng kǎlā OK.
example.english: On weekends we often go sing karaoke.
example.fact: Karaoke was invented in Japan in 1971 by musician Daisuke Inoue, who built a machine called the "Juke 8" so bar patrons could sing along to instrumental tracks; he never patented the invention, later saying he regretted missing out on what became a multibillion-dollar global industry.

components.note: 宀 (roof) depicts a house.
米 (rice) — a house full of rice suggested something deep and abundant, hidden within.
大 (a person) — a person discovering hidden depths gave 奥 its meaning 'mysterious, profound.'
其 (qí) is the phonetic element, only distantly related in sound to sī after centuries of drift.
斤 (axe) — 斯 originally meant 'to split, to cut apart' with an axe; the character was later borrowed for the demonstrative 'this, that' and for transliterating foreign names.
上 (top) — the upper edge pressing down
卜 — the lower edge, with a card squeezed between the two

example.hanzi: 那部电影获得了今年的奥斯卡最佳影片奖。
example.pinyin: nà bù diànyǐng huòdé le jīnnián de àosīkǎ zuìjiā yǐngpiàn jiǎng.
example.english: That film won this year's Oscar for Best Picture.
example.fact: The Oscar statuette is officially named the "Academy Award of Merit" and stands 13.5 inches tall, plated in 24-karat gold over britannium metal; the nickname "Oscar" is popularly traced to a 1930s Academy librarian who joked the statue resembled her uncle Oscar.

components.note: 攵 (an action) — ties to 故's sense of a cause or reason behind an action
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to 故's reading gù
阝 (mound, related to walls and terrain) — 障 describes something that blocks a path, like a wall.
章 (zhāng) gives a sound close to zhàng, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 电梯发生故障,大家只能走楼梯。
example.pinyin: diàntī fāshēng gùzhàng, dàjiā zhǐ néng zǒu lóutī.
example.english: The elevator broke down, so everyone had to take the stairs.
example.fact: Modern passenger elevators are required to have multiple independent safety systems, a design tradition dating back to Elisha Otis's 1854 public demonstration in New York, where he had the cable of his elevator platform deliberately cut to show his safety brake would stop it from falling.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
隹 (bird) suggests constant chatter, like a bird calling.
口 (mouth) below pictures a vendor calling out to sell goods, giving 售 its meaning 'to sell.'

example.hanzi: 这套房子正在以低价出售。
example.pinyin: zhè tào fángzi zhèngzài yǐ dījià chūshòu.
example.english: This apartment is currently being sold at a low price.
example.fact: The most expensive private residence ever sold, Antilia in Mumbai, is estimated to be worth over $1 billion and includes 27 floors, three helipads, and a staff of roughly 600 people to maintain it for a single family.

components.note: 金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 那条河里曾经淘出过金子。
example.pinyin: nà tiáo hé lǐ céngjīng táo chū guò jīnzi.
example.english: Gold was once panned from that river.
example.fact: The California Gold Rush began in January 1848 when James Marshall found flakes of gold in the American River; within two years the news had drawn over 300,000 people to California from around the world, permanently reshaping the region's population and economy.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伯 names a male relative, a person in the family.
白 (bái) gives the sound — close to bó, sharing the same initial and a similar rhyme.
寸 here depicts a hand.
良 pictures a goblet — together, a hand holding a ceremonial wine goblet, the image behind 爵's original meaning 'noble rank.'

example.hanzi: 那位伯爵拥有一座古老的城堡。
example.pinyin: nà wèi bójué yōngyǒu yī zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
example.english: That earl owns an ancient castle.
example.fact: The title "earl" is the oldest of the English peerage ranks, dating back to Anglo-Saxon England before the Norman Conquest of 1066, when it referred to a regional governor known as an "eorl" — a rank later slotted between duke and viscount in the modern nobility system.

components.note: 女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
巫 is traditionally read as a picture of a cross-shaped divining tool used by shamans in ritual — an image tied to its meaning 'wizard, shaman.'

example.hanzi: 故事里的女巫住在森林深处的小屋里。
example.pinyin: gùshi lǐ de nǚwū zhù zài sēnlín shēnchù de xiǎo wū lǐ.
example.english: The witch in the story lives in a cottage deep in the forest.
example.fact: During the Salem witch trials of 1692-1693 in colonial Massachusetts, roughly 200 people were accused of witchcraft and 20 were executed; historians have since proposed explanations ranging from ergot fungus poisoning of rye grain to social tensions among rival families in the small Puritan settlement.
